Header.CaseTitle: Metropolitan Property Holdings Ltd v Artisan Coffee Co Ltd
Header.AppealFrom: High Court of Justice, King's Bench Division

Counsel.Lead: Catherine Roberts KC; Michael Clarke (instructed by Clifford Chance LLP)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Respondent seeks relief from forfeiture and contends that the Appellant has waived the right to forfeit, that the alleged breaches have been remedied, and that it would be inequitable to grant possession.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Respondent's business was severely affected by the Covid-19 pandemic and subsequent trading conditions.
The Appellant accepted rent payments after becoming aware of the alleged breaches, constituting waiver.
The alterations complained of are reversible and do not materially affect the premises.
The Respondent has made substantial investment in the premises including a new shop front.
The Respondent has now cleared the rent arrears in full.

Contentions.item: The Appellant has waived the right to forfeit by accepting rent with knowledge of the breaches.
The breaches have been remedied and the arrears cleared.
It would be inequitable to grant forfeiture given the Respondent's substantial investment.
Relief from forfeiture should be granted on appropriate terms.

LegalBasis.item: Landlord and Tenant Act 1954, Part II
